title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
lede: Amazon is buying Decart's technology and team for a reported $7.5 billion, aiming its model optimization stack at Trainium chips rather than the world models Decart had been building.

points: The Decart Optimization Stack (DOS) makes AI models run better on many kinds of chips, not just Nvidia's.
Amazon says it has worked with Decart on Trainium since 2025; the deal is meant to speed that work up.
Anthropic reportedly tried to buy Decart at a similar price, and Nvidia, an investor at a $4 billion valuation, was rumored as a buyer.
Co-founders Dean Leitersdorf, Orian Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev join Amazon with their team.
TechCrunch compares it to Nvidia's $6.9 billion Mellanox purchase and Amazon's 2015 Annapurna Labs deal.

sections.text: Software that narrows the efficiency gap on non-Nvidia silicon could make Trainium, already used by Anthropic, a practical option for more AWS customers training and serving models.
